extracted.intended_audience: federal agency rulemaking officials, agency counsel, and regulatory staff responsible for petition-for-rulemaking procedures
extracted.subtask_description: Standards and recommended procedural requirements agencies should adopt for receiving, considering, and disposing of petitions for rulemaking under the Administrative Procedure Act, including publication, content guidance, notice, and internal management controls.

rubrics_metrics.name: Establish basic procedures for receipt, consideration, and prompt disposition
rubrics_metrics.description: Agencies should establish by rule basic procedures for the receipt, consideration, and prompt disposition of petitions for rulemaking.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is the overarching requirement: agencies should adopt procedural rules that govern how petitions are filed, reviewed, and concluded in a timely manner so the right to petition is meaningful.

rubrics_metrics.name: Specify filing address(es) and recommended petition contents
rubrics_metrics.description: Specify the address(es) for the filing of petitions and an outline of the recommended contents of the petition, such as the name, address, and telephone number of the petitioner, the statutory authority for the action requested, and a description of the rule to be issued, amended, or repealed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agencies should publish where petitions should be sent and advise petitioners what information to include (contact info, legal/statutory basis, clear description of requested rule action).

rubrics_metrics.name: Maintain a publicly available petition file
rubrics_metrics.description: Maintenance of a publicly available petition file.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agencies should keep and make accessible a file of petitions so interested persons can see submissions and agency handling of petitions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide prompt notification to petitioner with summary explanatory statement
rubrics_metrics.description: Provision for prompt notification to the petitioner of the action taken on the petition, with a summary explanatory statement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consistent with 5 U.S.C. § 555(e) and APA expectations, agencies should notify petitioners promptly (including denials) and summarize reasons for the agency's action.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publish petition procedures in accordance with APA public information provisions
rubrics_metrics.description: Agencies are expected to establish and publish such procedures in accordance with the public information section of the APA.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Publication of petition procedures ensures transparency and supports public participation; absence of published procedures undermines the right to petition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid excessive or rigid format requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not impose excessive or rigidly-enforced format requirements that impede filing of petitions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agencies should ensure format requirements do not unreasonably bar petitions; overly rigid requirements and failure to act promptly can undermine the public's right to file petitions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Make procedures applicable to all types of agency rules (where appropriate and feasible)
rubrics_metrics.description: Make their petition procedures expressly applicable to all types of rules the agency has authority to adopt, where appropriate and feasible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agencies should consider applying petition procedures broadly across the various rule types they issue, unless statutory or practical reasons counsel otherwise.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide guidance on data, argumentation, and information needed to consider petitions
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide guidance on the type of data, argumentation, or other information the agency needs to consider petitions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agencies should tell petitioners what evidence or analysis will assist the agency's evaluation, improving the quality and usefulness of petitions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notify interested persons that a petition has been filed and identify contact points for comments
rubrics_metrics.description: Develop effective methods for providing notice to interested persons that a petition has been filed and identify the agency office or official to whom inquiries and comments should be made.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agencies should publicize filed petitions and provide clear points of contact so stakeholders can follow and comment on petitions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Establish internal management controls to assure timely processing
rubrics_metrics.description: Establish internal management controls to assure the timely processing of petitions for rulemaking, including deadlines for completing interim actions and reaching conclusions on petitions and systems to monitor compliance with those deadlines.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agencies should set internal deadlines, track progress, and monitor adherence to timelines so petitions are processed within a reasonable time (per 5 U.S.C. § 555(b)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Regularly review and adopt measures ensuring the right to petition is meaningful
rubrics_metrics.description: Agencies should review their rulemaking petition procedures and practices and adopt measures that will ensure that the right to petition is a meaningful one.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Periodic review and improvement of procedures promotes public participation and aligns agency practice with the value Congress placed on petition rights.
